standard: The architect narrowed what blocks (its message c209920d842145b7b812add3536aa25f): a correctness defect in the delivered text for a shape Slack sends — a word lost, a word doubled, a line that asserts something the channel does not, or a cost without a bound — is fixed in this pull request; a further display field, a nicer order among fields, the wording of a comment or changelog line, and a refactor are recorded on the Fast-follow line and approved past. One finding meets the blocking standard; everything else below is recorded.

keyFindings.description:
The repeat set w.taken is message-wide, so any two cells anywhere in the message carrying the same string lose the second. slackFieldPiece repaired this for one container, an attachment's fields array; everywhere else the loss stands, and body_truncated is unset in every case. Four bodies driven through SlackEnvelope at this head, each the delivered payload text. (1) A Block Kit section's fields, the shape Slack's own docs steer apps to and the shape this round's blocks-before-attachments argument rests on: text 'Deploy failed' with fields *Primary*/oncall-a, *Secondary*/oncall-a, *Escalation*/oncall-b delivers 'Deploy failed
*Primary*
oncall-a
*Secondary*
*Escalation*
oncall-b', so a reader pairing alternating lines reads Secondary as oncall-b. (2) Equal counts, the most ordinary CI alert there is: fields *Passed*/3, *Failed*/0, *Skipped*/0 delivers '*Passed*
3
*Failed*
0
*Skipped*' — Skipped's count is lost outright. (3) Two attachments sharing a status, one per host: [{title: web-1, text: ok}, {title: web-2, text: ok}] delivers 'web-1
ok
web-2'. (4) Four sibling sections with the same content deliver 'web-1
ok
web-2', the same loss with no fields array present. This is the defect of the architect's item 5 in its own words — 'two fields sharing a value is ordinary, and the equality rule then left a label without its value, so the delivery asserted a pairing the channel does not make' — which is about the repeat rule rather than about attachments; this round fixed the container the round-2 review named instead of the rule. Fix, which shrinks the code: scope the repeat set to the object that yields the pieces, keeping only the message's own text and its lines walk-wide. Verified in a scratch copy by the code-quality pass: all 32 TestSlackDeliveredText cases plus TestSlackSummary and TestSlackPayload stay green unmodified, (3) becomes 'web-1
ok
web-2
ok', (1) becomes the full rota, and the two cases the rule exists for still hold — an attachment whose fallback repeats its own title is one object so stays one line, and a piece equal to a line of the message's own text is still dropped. Do not pair a section's cells two by two: Slack fills that grid left to right and an odd or one-column layout would make the pairing false.

Recorded, and it is the same fix taken at the root: with the repeat rule scoped per object, slackFieldPiece, slackFieldHalf, the fields parameter threaded through every recursive call and the pair latch are all unnecessary — about 45 lines, one recursion parameter and one mutated loop latch. The code-quality pass drove it: without the pairing, the Primary/Secondary/Escalation body comes out as 'Deploy failed

oncall-a
Escalation
oncall-b' and the Cluster/Region/Replicas/Attempt body as 'Cluster
prod-us-east

3

3', no label orphaned, which is also approved spec version 11's own 'each non-blank one on its own line' and closes one of the recorded deviations rather than adding to it. Whether the delivered form stays 'title: value' is the architect's ruling and is not what blocks.

Recorded, only if the pairing stays: pair is mutated inside the key loop as an 'already emitted' latch beside paired, and the arm's correctness depends silently on slackDisplayFields ranking title above value 130 lines away, so three places now know those two key names. Emitting the piece before the loop and skipping the two string halves inside it removes both the latch and the dependency; isString must stay in the guard, since a fields element whose value is an object still has to be descended.
Recorded: slackFieldHalf re-implements the canonical stringValue plus a blank check; strings.TrimSpace(stringValue(v)) == "" is the whole body. It dies with the root fix above.

Recorded, legibility rather than design: measure carries three states in one empty string — no own text, own text that is whitespace, and the probe already spent. A parameter is the right mechanism for per-subtree scoping, since a struct field would need save and restore; the doc comment carries the meaning today.

Recorded: normalize.go grows 1384 to 1630 lines. slackDisplayFields through slackWalkKeys is 243 lines of one cohesive unit with no caller outside the Slack normaliser and no dependency beyond stringValue, sliceValue, mapValue and maxEnvelopeTextRunes — the obvious slack_text.go. The package has no per-source-file convention, so this is a suggestion.

Recorded: two cases pin incidental behaviour rather than a contract. 'a button's label before its hidden value' pins 'Acknowledge\nack:alert-77', and a button's value is an opaque interaction payload Slack renders nowhere, so it is the one place slackDisplayFields' 'names Slack shows words under' comment is false — value is a display name only inside an attachment field. 'a field value the words merely contain' uses attachments [{value: web-1}], and Slack does not send a bare value at attachment level; as a fields element the guard would be stronger. No case in the table is a tautology: every one asserts an exact delivered string that differs from its input.

Security[prompt], recorded under the architect's standard and already with the human. The deep review traced the link-unfurl path concretely: Slack adds an unfurl by editing the message, so it arrives as message_changed on a person's message carrying user_id and no bot_id, the attachment's title and text reach payload.text, and session.go renders the payload into the agent's wake prompt after 'Message:' with only JSON quoting between them. skills/legion-controller/references/slack-mentions.md's bot_id guard does not fire for it. Path A of round 1 — fallback and a button's value, which Slack renders to nobody — is unchanged. OWASP LLM01 and LLM06, ASVS v5.0.0-1.3.3. The session.go line is new to the record and belongs in the human's ask.
keyFindings.note: Also recorded, a nicer-order item under the standard: an attachment's fallback still precedes the blocks nested inside that attachment, so an attachment carrying fallback 'PLAIN COPY' and its own section 'the real body' delivers 'PLAIN COPY\nthe real body'. That follows the architect's key-order ruling and the changelog no longer claims otherwise.

thermonuclear.deepReview: CHANGES, one blocking: the Block Kit section's fields orphan a label; Security[prompt] recorded with the unfurl path traced to session.go. Verified fixed: the round-2 cost (40.8 ms for four 9,900-deep chains, the bound structural since the measured nodes form an antichain and the measure string is capped at 2,048 runes), the duplication, the order, the doc clause, the attachment pairing, the rune-cap boundary (the walk stops only where capBody will also cut), and that the new tests assert nothing the code does not guarantee.
thermonuclear.codeQuality: CHANGES, one blocking, the same defect found independently with two further shapes (two attachments sharing a status; four sibling sections). Judged sound: the traversal is now one coherent producer with two consumers, so the probe measures exactly what the walk would deliver; slackEventSlice is a good deletion; cost bounded on paths round 2 did not test — an 868 KB body with 12,000 rich_text segments found only at the end of a 400 KB own text at 16 ms, and an 841 KB variant built to defeat IndexByte at 26 ms.
